clue.text: Aptly running after a vintage jade wallpaper

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: running colours or running dye move about, so the word before it is jumbled

parts.note: a jade is a worn-out old horse, a nag
the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Something apt dashing after an old green ornament on a patterned wall covering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the shuffled first word behind the old horse, though it opens the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Anaglypta is a trade name for embossed paper wall covering, often painted over, so it is a kind of decorative paper.

clue.text: God after new ways to inspire?

indicators.note: after says the word naming the god comes second, behind the abbreviation for new

parts.note: N is the standard abbreviation for new
Ares is the Greek god of war

explanation.surface: A question whether a god follows fresh paths to inspire people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspire' is meant literally, breathing in; NARES are the nostrils, the passages air is drawn through.
explanation.definitionFit: Nares is the anatomical term for nostrils, the openings through which breath is drawn into the body.

clue.text: A catch at international caught moving upwards

parts.note: taken as written
to nab is to catch
taken as written
I is the abbreviation for international
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A cricketer takes a catch in an international match, the ball still climbing.
explanation.definitionFit: Anabatic describes air currents or winds that rise up a slope, so the word means ascending.

clue.text: Ridge captured by dodgy Russians

indicators.note: the letters are held prisoner inside the following phrase

parts.note: the run of letters spans the two words

explanation.surface: A ridge of land seized by untrustworthy Russian forces.
explanation.definitionFit: A gyrus is one of the rounded convolutions on the surface of the brain, a raised fold between grooves.

clue.text: Pleasant African display ground supported by king and queen

parts.note: a lek is a patch where birds such as grouse gather to display
K is the chess abbreviation for king
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A pleasant showground in Africa held up by a royal couple.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supported by' puts the royal pair underneath the display ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Lekker is South African colloquial speech, from Afrikaans, for nice, tasty or enjoyable.

clue.text: Snooper small town's put up before beak

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word means reading it from the bottom upward

explanation.definitionFit: A prodnose is a meddlesome person who pokes into others' affairs, the same as a nosy busybody.

clue.text: Answer phone? Just the reverse, no?

indicators.note: doing exactly the opposite turns the order of the preceding phrase backwards

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: Someone told to answer the phone suggests doing the opposite instead.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark after 'no' flags that this is a word for refusal from another language.
explanation.definitionFit: Aikona is a South African interjection meaning not at all or certainly not, an emphatic refusal.

clue.text: Work alone in Perth upset with Australian weaver

parts.note: in Australian usage, as in Perth, to hat is to work alone like a solitary prospector

explanation.walkthrough: Perth is the one in Western Australia, not Scotland; a hatter was a miner who worked a claim alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A taha is a South African weaverbird, one of the finches that build woven nests.

clue.text: Winged figures set up in one capital

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.definitionFit: Amorini are cupids, small winged boy figures in Italian art, the plural of amorino.

clue.text: Tobacco pipe order incomplete, small shop's put out note

indicators.note: something incomplete lacks its final part, so a letter is cut from the end
putting something out ejects it, so a short musical syllable is removed

parts.note: a chit is a written order or voucher
a boutique is a small fashionable shop
ti, or te, is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A tobacco pipe order is left unfinished because a small shop has run out of a banknote.
explanation.definitionFit: A chibouque is a long Turkish tobacco pipe with a clay bowl, so it names a smoker's pipe.

clue.text: A mass with organ — my work of 2023?

parts.note: a mass of things is a great many
the ear is the organ of hearing

explanation.surface: A Mass with organ music, presented as the setter's composition for 2023.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests church music with the Mass, but it is the body part; one person's work over a year is the measure meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-year is a unit of labour equal to one person working for a full year, so one worker's output for 2023.

clue.text: Bring back hot principal girl

parts.note: H is the tap abbreviation for hot

explanation.surface: A call to bring back the sexy leading lady of a pantomime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'principal girl' is the pantomime role, but 'principal' belongs to the wordplay and 'girl' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Niamh is an Irish female given name, from the goddess of Irish legend, so it is a girl's name.

clue.text: A mostly sparse tree

parts.note: taken as written
rare means thinly spread or sparse

clue.text: Repeatedly carp about hard African language

clue.text: Check past distribution of beer around the country

indicators.note: around means the jumbled letters enclose what follows
distributing letters spreads them out into a new order

parts.note: the anagram fodder
UK is the abbreviation for the United Kingdom

explanation.walkthrough: 'past' marks an old sense: to rebuke once meant to check or restrain, not just to scold.
explanation.definitionFit: In obsolete usage rebuke meant to repress or hold back, which is what checking something does.

clue.text: Note deceit about pub coming up ready for new electrics?

parts.note: a bar is a pub

clue.text: Follower in church row between chapter and bishop

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for chapter

B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.walkthrough: 'row' wants to be a quarrel, fitting the church setting, but it is what you do with an oar.
explanation.definitionFit: A coarb was the successor of a saint as head of an Irish monastery, one who followed in office.

clue.text: ESA facility bundle terminal parts to skyrocket

explanation.definitionFit: Spacelab was the reusable laboratory module built by the European Space Agency and flown in the Shuttle bay.

clue.text: Messenger pigeon, one used in combined operations

explanation.walkthrough: 'Messenger pigeon' reads as one phrase, but the break comes after 'Messenger'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuncio is a papal envoy or ambassador, so he carries messages from the Pope.

clue.text: Fruit starter of clafoutis as cooked in batter

parts.note: clafoutis is a French fruit batter pudding
à la means in the manner of, as a dish is cooked
to batter is to bash

explanation.surface: Fruit is the first thing into a clafoutis, which is cooked in batter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'batter' fits the pudding but is the verb to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A calabash is the gourd fruit of the calabash tree or vine, often dried as a vessel.

clue.text: Grew old around father with late onset disease

indicators.note: around means the first word encloses the following one
a late onset means the opening letter arrives at the end instead

parts.note: wox is an old past tense of wax, to grow
pater is Latin, and old schoolboy slang, for father

explanation.surface: Someone aged around their father and then fell ill with something that arrives late in life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grew old' looks like ageing; 'old' marks an archaic verb form instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Water-pox is an old name for chickenpox, a contagious viral illness causing watery blisters.

clue.text: Take all nine with one running up — underarm

indicators.note: running up in a down clue means the whole string reads from the bottom

parts.note: R, recipe, is the prescription abbreviation for take
taken as written
IX is nine in Roman numerals
a means one

explanation.definitionFit: Axillar means relating to the axilla, the armpit, so it describes what lies beneath the arm.

clue.text: Severe second illness for Macbeth

parts.note: cruel means harsh or severe

explanation.walkthrough: Macbeth stands for Scotland: the answer is a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Cruels is a Scots name for scrofula, the tuberculous swelling of the neck glands, so a Scottish disease.

clue.text: Row about time which US uses for complete change of solution?
